title: Integration description
description: What <program> describe prints on its standard output, once, as one JSON document, and exits 0: the integration's name, the domains it works with, the settings it takes and the roles it plays. It takes no settings and reaches no network. A program that fails prints nothing on standard output, one line on standard error describing what failed, and exits non-zero. A reader expands any declared integration into its definitions from this document alone.

name.description: The integration's name: the key a machine's configuration declares it under, unless the machine chooses another, and so the name of what it defines there. The key is the name of the gateway's credential and of the program qory-<key> of this repository's, so the name is the credential's grammar without the dot.

title.description: A human name, for a form or a listing.

description.description: A sentence or two on what the integration does, for a form or a listing.

domains.description: The domains the integration works with, each a domain name, such as software. When the integration names no domain, the field is absent, never an empty list.

program_version.description: The program's own version, as it was built.

settings.description: A JSON Schema, draft 2020-12, of the settings document: an object. A property marked writeOnly is a secret: a form shows it as one, written and never read back, a log leaves it out, and it stays off every command line. A secret is a property of the settings object itself, never a nested one, and a secret <name> has a setting <name>_file, a file that contains it, which is passed on a command line in its place.

roles.description: The roles the program plays, by name. A reader expands the roles it knows and leaves the others as they are.

credential.description: The gateway's credential adapter. The program is started as <program> credential --settings <json> -- <argument> and prints the gateway's credential document.

argument.description: A regular expression, RE2, the policy's argument must match whole: the definition's argument.

hosts.description: The hosts the adapter answers for: the definition's hosts, the most an answer may claim.
